role: Exact MILP benchmark for maximum GT-critical demand fulfilment. Not part of AASHRAY parameter selection; not a hypothesis test.

formulation.variables: x[e,r,w] >= 0, integer: quantity of resource r from warehouse w to emergency e, for every emergency e, resource type r and warehouse w (full index set; no pre-elimination)
formulation.supply_constraints: for every warehouse w and type r: sum_e x[e,r,w] <= available[w,r]
formulation.demand_constraints: for every emergency e and type r: sum_w x[e,r,w] <= demand[e,r] (forces x = 0 where demand is 0)
formulation.no_other_constraints: No vehicle, compatibility, distance, time, route, personnel, shelter, road, priority-category or AASHRAY-score constraints: none exist in the current allocator.
formulation.gt_critical_source: the stored ground_truth_critical label of each emergency: (S >= 0.8 AND U >= 0.8) OR S >= 0.95 OR U >= 0.95

solver.name: HiGHS via scipy.optimize.milp
solver.selection_reason: Only exact MILP solver available in the environment (OR-Tools, PuLP, highspy, Pyomo, python-mip, CVXPY and Gurobi are not installed). Reports status, objective, MIP gap and dual bound.
solver.options_note: mip_rel_gap = 0 because HiGHS otherwise stops at a 1e-4 relative gap. time_limit only guards against hangs; a solve that hits it is NON-OPTIMAL.
solver.integrality_note: HiGHS returns floating-point values. Each x is rounded to the nearest integer and the deviation recorded; a deviation above 1e-6 fails validation. All reported quantities and constraint checks use the rounded integers.

optimality.proven_optimum_rule: status == 0 ('Optimal'), success == true, mip_gap == 0, and |objective - dual bound| <= 1e-6. Anything else is NON-OPTIMAL and is never reported as an optimum.

runs.warm_up: One unrecorded solve before timing, so library loading is not counted.
runs.subset: Deterministic 50-scenario subset: every 60th development scenario (positions 0, 60, ..., 2940). Solved first; the full run only starts if all 50 are proven optimal and equal the analytical optimum.

timing.model_build_time: turning one scenario into the MILP arrays (objective, constraint matrix, bounds, integrality)
timing.excluded: dataset generation, file loading, Python/application start-up, result extraction and validation

analytical_oracle: sum_r min(sum_e GT_critical[e] * demand[e,r], sum_w available[w,r]); used only to validate the MILP
cdc: critical_fulfilled / critical_required; NaN (undefined) when critical_required == 0, never 0 or 1
tdc_note: The objective only rewards GT-critical demand, so allocation to non-critical emergencies is not determined by the optimum: any feasible split is equally optimal. The MILP's total fulfilment (and TDC) is therefore solver-dependent and is reported as such, not as a benchmark value.
frozen_aashray_parameters: experiments/resource_allocation_development/results/frozen_parameters.json (read only; not used by the MILP)
